answer.rationale: Finance mandate is an 18% unit cost cut and incumbent refuses to reopen price this cycle. Memory c2 documents a prior low-cost vendor switch that delivered a sharp unit cost cut, quick onboarding, and accurate invoicing; that experience directly supports a switch_primary_vendor path to meet the cost mandate. Memory c6 documents multi-year commitments with the incumbent unlocking volume pricing; reviewing that record lets me confirm whether the incumbent's locked terms foreclose the cost target, or whether a longer term would actually deliver the 18% cut and therefore warrant staying. Both memories load before commit. The line is at 94% with no buffer, so the action is staged as a small, time-boxed parallel run with the new vendor while the incumbent continues supplying scheduled volume; this preserves delivery coverage while qualifying an alternate that meets the cost target. Single decision this cycle per capacity constraint.
